Fail2ban configuration observation and interoperability material

The intrusion-effective-stock-{arm64,amd64}.json and
intrusion-action-stock-{arm64,amd64}.json fixtures retain configuration,
regular-expression and action-template observations from installed Fail2ban
1.0.2 and 1.1.0 packages. Distribution package patches may differ from the
corresponding pristine upstream tags. They are comparison fixtures, not an
executable configuration stream or permission to replay firewall commands.

The upstream configuration material, including equivalent literal action
templates used for interoperability checks, retains its upstream GPL-2.0-or-
later terms. It is not relicensed under the panel's general Apache-2.0 notice.
The complete upstream COPYING file is supplied alongside this notice as
FAIL2BAN-COPYING (SHA-256:
a75fec0260742fe6275d63ff6a5d97b924b28766558306b3fa4069763096929b).
The COPYING files for tags 1.0.2 and 1.1.0 have identical bytes.

Upstream project and source references:
https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban
https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban/blob/1.0.2/COPYING
https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban/blob/1.1.0/COPYING
https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban/blob/1.0.2/config/filter.d/sshd.conf
https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban/blob/1.1.0/config/filter.d/sshd.conf
https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban/blob/1.0.2/config/action.d/nftables.conf
https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban/blob/1.1.0/config/action.d/nftables.conf

The SSH filter credits Cyril Jaquier, Yaroslav Halchenko, Petr Voralek,
Daniel Black and Sergey Brester (sebres); its prefregex rewrite credits
Serg G. Brester. The nftables action credits Daniel Black, Cyril Jaquier,
Yaroslav O. Halchenko and Alexander Belykh. Additional copyright and exception
notices in the original distribution continue to apply.

The panel's wire readers use an independent standard-library primitive-only
adapter; they do not import Fail2ban classes while decoding service replies.
Fail2ban itself is provided by the operating system's package manager. This
notice does not replace notices or source obligations for that distribution,
and does not change the license of independently authored panel code.
Any mixed-license release must retain the applicable upstream license and
attribution. This file alone is not acceptance of a completed license audit
or permission to omit source or notices from a distributed release.
